final_dataset_pre_quality_gate.evidence_quote: gic Fever with Renal Syndrome (HFRS), occurred during the Korean War in the early 1950s. The causative virus, *Hantaan virus*, was later isolated in 1978 from rodents near the Hantaan River in Korea. Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome (HPS) was identified in the Americas during a 1993 outbreak in the US Four Corners region. In May 2026, an outbreak aboard the MV Hondius cruise ship traveling from Argentina to Cape Verde brought renewed global attention: three passengers died and the *Andes strain* — the only hantavirus known to transmit person-to-person — was confirmed in evacuated patients. Investigators traced the source to a bird-watching tour in Ushuaia, Argentina. Symptômes Initial (Prodromal) Symptoms: Fever, fatigue, severe muscle aches (especially in large muscle groups), headache, dizziness, chills. Gastrointestinal Symptoms: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain. For Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome (HPS): Rapid onset of shortness of breath, cough, and fluid in the lungs, leading to severe respiratory distress. For Hemorrhagic Fever with Renal Syndrome (HFRS): Low blood pressure, acute kidney failure, and hemorrhage (bleeding). Transmission Hantavirus is primarily transmitted to humans through the inhalation of aerosolized particles from the urine, droppings, or saliva of infected rodents. Direct contact with infected rodents, or a rodent bite, can also transmit the virus, but this is less common. Most hantavirus strains do not spread person-to-person. The notable exception is the *Andes virus* found in southern South America, which can transmit between people through close, prolonged contact and was confirmed in the 2026 MV Hondius cruise ship outbreak.

quarantined_records.evidence_quote: gic Fever with Renal Syndrome (HFRS), occurred during the Korean War in the early 1950s. The causative virus, *Hantaan virus*, was later isolated in 1978 from rodents near the Hantaan River in Korea. Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome (HPS) was identified in the Americas during a 1993 outbreak in the US Four Corners region. In May 2026, an outbreak aboard the MV Hondius cruise ship traveling from Argentina to Cape Verde brought renewed global attention: three passengers died and the *Andes strain* — the only hantavirus known to transmit person-to-person — was confirmed in evacuated patients. Investigators traced the source to a bird-watching tour in Ushuaia, Argentina. Symptômes Initial (Prodromal) Symptoms: Fever, fatigue, severe muscle aches (especially in large muscle groups), headache, dizziness, chills. Gastrointestinal Symptoms: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain. For Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome (HPS): Rapid onset of shortness of breath, cough, and fluid in the lungs, leading to severe respiratory distress. For Hemorrhagic Fever with Renal Syndrome (HFRS): Low blood pressure, acute kidney failure, and hemorrhage (bleeding). Transmission Hantavirus is primarily transmitted to humans through the inhalation of aerosolized particles from the urine, droppings, or saliva of infected rodents. Direct contact with infected rodents, or a rodent bite, can also transmit the virus, but this is less common. Most hantavirus strains do not spread person-to-person. The notable exception is the *Andes virus* found in southern South America, which can transmit between people through close, prolonged contact and was confirmed in the 2026 MV Hondius cruise ship outbreak.

anomaly_results.evidence_summary: gic Fever with Renal Syndrome (HFRS), occurred during the Korean War in the early 1950s. The causative virus, *Hantaan virus*, was later isolated in 1978 from rodents near the Hantaan River in Korea. Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome (HPS) was identified in the Americas during a 1993 outbreak in the US Four Corners region. In May 2026, an outbreak aboard the MV Hondius cruise ship traveling from Argentina to Cape Verde brought renewed global attention: three passengers died and the *Andes strain* — the only hantavirus known to transmit person-to-person — was confirmed in evacuated patients. Investigators traced the source to a bird-watching tour in Ushuaia, Argentina. Symptômes Initial (Prodromal) Symptoms: Fever, fatigue, severe muscle aches (especially in large muscle groups), headache, dizziness, chills. Gastrointestinal Symptoms: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain. For Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome (HPS): Rapid onset of shortness of breath, cough, and fluid in the lungs, leading to severe respiratory distress. For Hemorrhagic Fever with Renal Syndrome (HFRS): Low blood pressure, acute kidney failure, and hemorrhage (bleeding). Transmission Hantavirus is primarily transmitted to humans through the inhalation of aerosolized particles from the urine, droppings, or saliva of infected rodents. Direct contact with infected rodents, or a rodent bite, can also transmit the virus, but this is less common. Most hantavirus strains do not spread person-to-person. The notable exception is the *Andes virus* found in southern South America, which can transmit between people through close, prolonged contact and was confirmed in the 2026 MV Hondius cruise ship outbreak.

human_review_items.evidence_summary: gic Fever with Renal Syndrome (HFRS), occurred during the Korean War in the early 1950s. The causative virus, *Hantaan virus*, was later isolated in 1978 from rodents near the Hantaan River in Korea. Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome (HPS) was identified in the Americas during a 1993 outbreak in the US Four Corners region. In May 2026, an outbreak aboard the MV Hondius cruise ship traveling from Argentina to Cape Verde brought renewed global attention: three passengers died and the *Andes strain* — the only hantavirus known to transmit person-to-person — was confirmed in evacuated patients. Investigators traced the source to a bird-watching tour in Ushuaia, Argentina. Symptômes Initial (Prodromal) Symptoms: Fever, fatigue, severe muscle aches (especially in large muscle groups), headache, dizziness, chills. Gastrointestinal Symptoms: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain. For Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome (HPS): Rapid onset of shortness of breath, cough, and fluid in the lungs, leading to severe respiratory distress. For Hemorrhagic Fever with Renal Syndrome (HFRS): Low blood pressure, acute kidney failure, and hemorrhage (bleeding). Transmission Hantavirus is primarily transmitted to humans through the inhalation of aerosolized particles from the urine, droppings, or saliva of infected rodents. Direct contact with infected rodents, or a rodent bite, can also transmit the virus, but this is less common. Most hantavirus strains do not spread person-to-person. The notable exception is the *Andes virus* found in southern South America, which can transmit between people through close, prolonged contact and was confirmed in the 2026 MV Hondius cruise ship outbreak.
